# `Q-1-12` — Invalid Enum Value

> A value is not one of the choices the schema's enumeration
> allows.

## What this means

Some Quarto configuration fields accept only a fixed set of
values. Output format names, theme names, engine names, and many
other configuration choices are restricted this way. The schema
calls this restriction an *enumeration* — literally the list of
values it will accept.

This error fires when your YAML's value passes the basic type
check (the field expects a string and you provided a string), but
the value itself isn't on the allowed list. The error message
includes both the value you provided and the full list of
acceptable values.

## Why this happens

Three common cases:

- **Typo in the value.** `html5` instead of `html`, `gfm-md` instead
  of `gfm`, or capitalization mismatches like `HTML` for `html`.
  Enum matching is case-sensitive.
- **A value valid in a different release.** A name that worked in
  Quarto 1 might not exist in Quarto 2, or a third-party format
  may not be installed.
- **Confusion between similar fields.** Providing a theme name in
  a slot that wants an output format, or the other way around.

## How to fix

The error message lists every allowed value for the property. Pick
the one you meant, paying attention to spelling and case. If none
of them is what you wanted, the property may not be the right
place for what you are configuring — check the documentation for
the configuration block the property belongs to.

## Related

- [`Q-1-11`](Q-1-11.qmd) — type mismatch: the value has the wrong type entirely,
  not just an unrecognized choice.
- [`Q-1-14`](Q-1-14.qmd) — string pattern mismatch: a less strict version where
  the schema accepts strings matching a pattern rather than an
  exact list.
